subject: Animation
title: Ease In and Ease Out: Natural Acceleration
description: A fast breakdown of Ease In and Ease Out: Natural Acceleration for builders.

hook.text: Nothing in nature starts or stops instantly. Everything accelerates from stillness and decelerates to a stop.

buildup.text: Ease in means drawings are closer together at the start. Ease out means they cluster near the end.

discovery.text: This spacing creates the illusion of natural acceleration and deceleration in animated movement.

twist.text: Linear motion — equal spacing between frames — looks mechanical and is only used for robots or machines.

climax.text: Ease in and ease out is what separates motion that feels alive from motion that feels programmed.

punchline.text: Life accelerates and decelerates. Only machines move at constant speed.

quiz.question: What creates the illusion of natural motion in animation?
options: Drawing all frames with equal spacing between positions
Clustering drawings closer at the start and end of motion to simulate acceleration and deceleration
Adding motion blur to every frame

details.summary: Ease in and ease out means objects accelerate when starting and decelerate when stopping rather than moving at constant speed. This mirrors real physics where nothing starts or stops instantaneously.
details.whyItMatters: Constant-speed movement looks robotic and lifeless. Easing creates the illusion of weight and natural physics, transforming mechanical frame sequences into believable organic motion.
takeaways: Objects should accelerate into movement and decelerate to a stop
Constant-speed motion looks mechanical and unnatural
More frames at the start and end of movement create easing

faq.question: How do animators create ease in and ease out?
faq.answer: By spacing frames closer together at the beginning and end of a movement, and farther apart in the middle. Clustered frames create slow movement; spread frames create fast movement, mimicking natural acceleration curves.

faq.question: When should animation NOT use ease in and ease out?
faq.answer: For sudden impacts like a ball bouncing off a wall, or mechanical movements like a clock hand. Instant direction changes and constant-speed motion are appropriate when depicting non-organic or high-energy physics.
